content.introduction: The United States boasts the world's largest economy, with an estimated GDP of over 31 trillion dollars by early 2026, growing at an average rate of 2.6 percent per year. The country's per capita income is USD 45,284, the highest in the OECD. The national debt has passed $40 trillion, doubling in a decade. The population is projected to reach 358,633,000 by 2030, with a density of 89.4 persons per square mile. The Gini coefficient for 2024 indicates medium inequality at 41.8, and the Human Development Index (HDI) for 2023 is 0.938, ranking 17th globally.

## Economy

[change | change source]

Main article: Economy of the United States



The US boasts of the biggest economy in the world. By the early 2026, its Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is estimated to be more than 31 trillion dollars. The economy is improving at an average growth of 2.6 percent per year. [...] Today, the United States is one of the world's most ethnically mixed and multicultural nations. It is the product of large-scale immigration from many countries. The U.S. economy is the largest national economy in the world, with an estimated 2020 gross domestic product (GDP) of US$ 20.9 trillion (about a quarter of worldwide GDP).

## Geography and environment

[change | change source]

Main article: Geography of the United States [...] The United States of America (USA or U.S.A.), also known as the United States (U.S. or US) or America, is a country that is located in North America. It is made of 50 states, a federal district (Washington, D.C., the District of Columbia), and some other territories and insular areas. Forty-eight of the states are connected (Contiguous United States), and they are bordered by Canada to the north and Mexico to the south.
